newsitem.title: USA: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Investors keep to sidelines.
newsitem.headline: U.S. OPTIONS FOCUS/Investors keep to sidelines.

text.p: Index options trading was thin Wednesday as investors continued to avoid placing big bets amid a heavy calendar of economic data this week and the U.S. presidential election next week.
"It's been slow the last three or four days. Everybody is waiting for the employment figures or the election," said Rod Jamieson at EVEREN Securities.
The October U.S. employment report is due Friday before the market opens and the election is November 5.
On Wednesday, the Federal Reserve issued its Beige Book of national economic activity.
September personal income and consumption data are due Thursday along with weekly jobless claims and the October Chicago Purchasing Managers Index.
Traders said the market's choppiness would normally provide a boost in options activity but this time around many investors preferred to sit on the sidelines.
Jamieson said sharp swings in some individual stocks did not touch off heavier options trading there either.
"I would think with some of these great swings we've been having we'd get more action, but it just hasn't been turning out that way," he said.
By 1430 CST (2030 GMT), just 132,763 index options had traded on the Chicago Board Options Exchange (CBOE), with put turnover topping call turnover 82,744 to 50,019.
The most active index option on the CBOE was the S&P 100 index November 675 put, which traded roughly 11,830 contracts. It had open interest of nearly 17,000.
The November 670 put, with open interest of 20,200, traded about 9,475 contracts.
With the OEX weakening in afternoon trade, the November 675 put added 3/4 to 9-3/8 and the 670 rose 3/8 to 7-3/8.
At 1510 CST (2110 GMT), the OEX was down a point at about 675.50, the S&P 500 index .SPX was off a touch at about 701 and the Dow industrials .DJI were down 14 points at 5,993.
In the SPX, where overall put volume continued to solidly outpace call volume, two of the busiest options were calls.
The SPX January 710 call, which had open interest of five, traded 4,600 contracts and the November 710 call, with open interest of 10,500, traded 3,635.
But the December 650 put traded 6,230 contracts. It had open interest of 45,810 and was up 1/2 at 4-1/2. -Gregory Crawford, 312/408-8750/Email: derivatives@reuters.com
